records.quote: I was in want of boots, of clothes, of the whole human varnish that makes a man perceptible.
records.paraphrase: The shadow explains that clothing was what made him perceptible as a man.

records.quote: So she began, by degrees, to question him about the most difficult things she could think of, and which she herself could not have answered
records.paraphrase: The princess systematically tests the suitor's knowledge with hard questions.

records.quote: So then, it has actually gone last night, and not come again.
records.paraphrase: The learned man discovers his shadow has detached and departed from him.

records.quote: after the lapse of eight days he observed, to his great joy, that a new shadow came in the sunshine
records.paraphrase: A new shadow grows back for the man in the warm lands.

records.quote: Nay, this is going too far!\u201d said the learned man. \u201cI will not have it; I will not do it!
records.paraphrase: The learned man refuses the shadow's demand that he pose as its shadow.

records.quote: she almost pierced him through with her eyes
records.paraphrase: The princess, who sees too clearly, examines the shadow intently as she falls in love.

records.quote: thou must submit to be called SHADOW by all and everyone; thou must not say that thou hast ever been a man
records.paraphrase: The shadow demands the man permanently take on the role and identity of a shadow.

records.quote: I never imagined that one's old shadow could come again as a man.
records.paraphrase: The learned man remarks on the strangeness of a shadow becoming a man.

records.quote: when the sun rose, and when the sun went down, I became so strangely great; in the moonlight I was very near being more distinct than yourself
records.paraphrase: The shadow describes how its size and distinctness changed with the sun and moon.

records.quote: Do you not know your old shadow? You certainly thought I should never more return.
records.paraphrase: The lost shadow returns years later, now embodied as a wealthy man.

records.quote: The learned man heard nothing of all this\u2014for they had deprived him of life.
records.paraphrase: The learned man is put to death while the shadow marries the princess.

records.quote: the shadow was master, and the master was the shadow
records.paraphrase: The roles reverse so that the shadow becomes master and the man becomes the shadow.

records.quote: This annoyed him: not so much because the shadow was gone, but because he knew there was a story about a man without a shadow.
records.paraphrase: The man is annoyed by the loss and worried about resembling an existing tale.

criteria.rationale: The tale is a fairy-tale allegory. References to the sun and moon changing a shadow's size, or clothing making a man 'perceptible,' are poetic/magical rather than materially represented scientific facts, theories, or natural processes. No genuine science drives the story.
No device, technique, engineered system, or invention materially affects the setting, problem, or outcome. The story's transformations are magical, not technological.
The story is set in an ordinary contemporary-to-Andersen milieu (warm lands, cold northern lands). There is no speculative future, remote past, or temporal displacement.

The premise of a shadow gaining autonomy is developed into consequences (master/servant role reversal, the shadow demanding the man permanently play the shadow). However, the premise is fantastical/allegorical rather than an identifiable scientific, technological, or historical premise, so materiality and fit are uncertain.

The princess questioning the suitor and 'seeing too clearly' is generic testing/scrutiny, not systematic hypothesis-testing, measurement, or evidential revision that materially drives understanding. This is ordinary interrogation, not the scientific method.
There are no other planets, dimensions, nonordinary cosmic environments, or visitors from them. The animated shadow is a supernatural double within an ordinary earthly setting, not a cosmic visitor.

The learned man's execution is a personal misfortune, not a natural, technological, cosmic, biological, or human-caused large-scale disaster. There is no catastrophe of broad scale, actual, impending, or remembered.

candidates.description: A man's shadow detaches from him, gains independent existence, eventually acquires a body and full human status, and progressively supplants its former master\u2014rising socially to marry a princess while reducing the original man to the role of a shadow and finally having him executed.

novelty.rationale: The premise that a shadow can separate, persist independently, incarnate as a man, and reverse the master/shadow relation is a totalizing departure from empirical norms that reorganizes the entire storyworld's social and ontological logic.

cognitive_validation.rationale: The story offers a quasi-systematic, immanent account: the shadow attributes its transformation to its nature revealed near Poesy, and its manhood is explained through the acquisition of clothing/the 'human varnish that makes a man perceptible,' framing perceptibility as a social/material condition rather than invoking deities. However, the mechanism remains fairy-tale enchantment with no consistent immanent law, so the cognitive coherence is partial and not clearly nonsupernatural.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The detached shadow is not an incidental device; it governs the whole plot arc from separation to the inversion of roles and the man's execution, determining the overriding narrative logic.

estrangement.rationale: The learned man's own remark that he 'never imagined that one's old shadow could come again as a man' marks the reader-facing contrast with empirical expectation, while the storyworld consequences (loss, regrowth, return, role reversal, execution) show the novum's totalizing reach.

candidates.description: A princess afflicted with seeing too clearly, able to perceive that the shadow-man casts no shadow, whose condition is said to be curable by the waters.

novelty.rationale: The idea of a person who 'sees too well' as an affliction is an unusual difference, but it is a localized trait rather than a world-altering condition.

cognitive_validation.rationale: No systematic or immanent account of this perceptual condition is provided beyond fairy-tale assertion.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The princess's clear sight is an incidental complication that the shadow easily deflects; it does not govern the overriding narrative logic, which is driven by the shadow's usurpation.

estrangement.rationale: The princess piercing the shadow with her eyes and her systematic questioning gesture toward her unusual perception, but these remain peripheral to the central novum.
